title: POSTCARDS FROM THE OTHER TOWN · V
venue: Arthur's site · a romance the strip never ran · eight cards · Box 19
logline: Hers: the front is the northbound route drawn as a single line across the card with the lighthouse at the bottom and the city at the top and the bus a dot two-thirds up; the back, one word. The sentence changes direction.

panels.composition: The postcard's front: a single line running the height of the card from a tiny lighthouse at the bottom to a tiny city at the top with a dot two-thirds of the way up.

image.prompt: two-color coastal weekly illustration, a single vertical line from a tiny lighthouse at the bottom of a card to a tiny city at the top with a small dot two thirds up, no words legible

panels.name: Front

panels.composition: The postcard's back: the message side with the fifth word legible, very small.

image.prompt: the back of a postcard drawn in ink, a divided back with an address side and a message side, the handwriting rendered as strokes with one word left legible, a small stamp with a tiny numeral in its corner, the fifth word written very small, the only legible word on the card is its
image.notes: Two-thirds up: the bus is past her and not yet there. The one legible word: its. Stamp numeral: IV.

panels.name: Back

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink for the fronts; the backs in a stranger's hand, drawn as shapes but for one word each
art.palette: the fronts in the coastal weekly's two-color; the stamps in one color each
art.paper: cardstock cut to postcard size, drawn both sides, photographed as spreads
